acceptance_criteria.criterion: Scrolling down the queue page and waiting for a 5-second refresh cycle does not reset the viewport to the top.
`window.scrollY` is used as the save/restore target (not `container.scrollTop`, since `#orch-queue-container` has no overflow CSS — the viewport is the scrolling context).
The scroll position is restored after all post-render DOM manipulation (action button injection, event listener attachment) completes, not just after the innerHTML assignment.
The `QueueEntry` interface in `types.ts` includes a `projectExists: boolean` field.
`getQueue()` populates `projectExists` from `projectStatus.exists` for every returned entry.
The "View Project" button is NOT rendered when `projectExists` is `false`, even if `effectiveStatus === 'started'`.
The "View Project" button IS rendered when `projectExists` is `true` and `entry.expectedSlug` is truthy.
A unit test covers both the `projectExists: true` and `projectExists: false` cases for `getQueue()` output.
Existing tests continue to pass without modification (no regressions).

Failing test: `tests/gui/orchestrator-view.test.ts > renderOrchestrator — AC-4: row actions > shows project link for started entries`.

Root cause: `makeEntry()` in orchestrator-view.test.ts does not include `projectExists` in its default shape. When the test calls `makeEntry({ effectiveStatus: 'started', expectedSlug: 'my-project' })`, the resulting entry has `projectExists: undefined`. The updated condition in orchestrator.js (`entry.projectExists === true && entry.expectedSlug`) evaluates to `false`, so no `.orch-project-link` is rendered.
This is a regression against AC-9 ('Existing tests continue to pass without modification'). The Developer claim that AC-9 is met is incorrect — one pre-existing test now fails.
